children: Netflix (NFLX) Q3 revenue $12.874B (+12% YoY), net income $3.664B, EPS $0.87, operating margin 34.6%, free cash flow ~$2.884B. Q4 rev guide ~$13.44B, EPS $0.67; 2026 ad revenue trimmed to ~$2.7B.
Netflix repurchased $4.8B in the quarter — about 63.9M shares, its biggest quarterly buyback. Quarter-end gross debt: $15.3B; cash and equivalents: $8.2B.
Netflix cut its 2026 ad revenue forecast to ~$2.7B from ~$3.0B due to slower ad product rollout. 2026 total revenue guided to $51.1B; operating margin targeted at 31.5%.
Netflix (NFLX) will cut about 1,000 jobs, ~6% of staff. Company says layoffs will pressure margins, citing lower viewership, rising competition and profit impact.
Large Nov.20 NFLX $70 put sale ~ $2M and >3,500 $80 calls bought for Friday expiry; $80 calls need ~20% stock rise by Friday to breakeven.
Netflix (NFLX) tops 325M subscribers, monthly churn ~2% in September; price hikes met expectations. Investors remain cautious about sustaining long-term audience growth without bigger content buys.
Netflix (NFLX) plans to expand its ad-supported tier to 15 more countries in 2027 and says it’s investing in ads, programmatic CTV deals, and third-party content partnerships.
Needham projects Netflix ad revenue near $3B for the year, about double prior year, with ~80% ad margins. Firm notes large unsold long-form ad inventory and competition from YouTube, TikTok, Reels.
Co-CEO Greg Peters said U.S. engagement at Netflix (NFLX) is solid but can improve; he cited holiday NFL games, Emily in Paris final season and Brad Pitt film as upcoming viewership drivers.
Netflix (NFLX) hired Peter Rice. Analyst notes Rice may shift programming toward more commercial, mass-appeal films and series to support subscriber growth and revenue potential.
